sentences.text: If you cook a pan over an open fire, you have the simplest stove there is.
But the smoke has nowhere to go, so it rises and spreads across the ceiling.
Then it banks down the walls until it floods the whole room.
The air turns toxic, because carbon monoxide passes 400 parts per million, enough for a headache within 1 to 2 hours.
So you box the fire in iron and run a pipe at least 3 feet above the roof, and the smoke leaves.
But now the pipe pulls air in so hard that the fire roars and the gauge races into the red.
So you turn a damper, a flap in the pipe, to slow the air, and the gauge falls.
But the heat still races straight up the pipe and out of the roof.
So you put an oven beside the fire, and the hot gas loops around it before it leaves.
And the pipe on top is called a flue.
Air comes in at the front and feeds the fire, then the hot gas loops around the oven and up the flue.
A hot oven bakes bread at around 230 degrees Celsius, though it has no thermostat.
And a cuisinière is not only a stove.
In French, cuisinière means both a cooking stove and a woman who cooks.
Add a kettle, a pot of stew and a cap on the chimney.
Congratulations, you have built a cookstove.
